chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A'ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Abu Ja'far<sup>asws</sup>, having said:

key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: Our companions — a collective reference to trusted narrators within the Shia scholarly circle
key_terms.السَّكِينَةُ: Tranquillity — the divine peace referenced in Quran 48:4, here interpreted by the Imam as being equivalent to iman
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: Faith — the iman (belief) that constitutes the true nature of the sakinah descending upon believers
key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: A number — an unspecified plurality of reliable transmitters forming the opening link of the sanad
key_terms.قَالَ: He said — the standard Arabic marker indicating the beginning of the matn attributed directly to the Imam

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir (AS) say is the meaning of 'al-sakinah' (tranquillity) in Surah al-Fath (48:4)?
ai.summary: In this concise exegetical statement, Imam Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) identifies 'al-sakinah' — the divine tranquillity referenced in Surah al-Fath (48:4) — as being iman (faith) itself. This interpretation, transmitted through a chain reaching Muhammad Bin Muslim, positions faith as the very substance of the spiritual peace that Allah descends into the hearts of believers. The equating of sakinah with iman carries significant theological weight, grounding inner serenity not in circumstance but in the believer's creedal and devotional state.
